answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging every identity a stake that grows with the value it touches: a new agent may pick one walnut from the orchard for free, but harvesting a whole row requires locking collateral and building a public atlas of its past deals. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand believable histories, while one honest agent's record compounds. The attack only pays if the harvest exceeds the locked collateral and the time spent faking a reputation.
